chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man fled with his wealth from the Zakat, and he bought with it a piece of land or a house. Is there anything upon him regarding it? He (peace be upon him) said: No. And if he made it into ornaments or carvings, there is nothing upon him regarding it. And what he prevented himself from of his own surplus is more than what he prevented from the Right of Allah, if it were to be in it.
ai.seo_question: Does a person who flees with their wealth to avoid Zakat have to pay Zakat again if they buy property with it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that wealth used to 'flee' from Zakat is not subject to double taxation, even if converted into fixed assets like land or jewelry, as the act of preservation itself serves as a form of consumption. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the obligation is tied to the specific cycle of wealth accumulation, and withholding voluntary charity (Sadaqah) is considered a greater deprivation than fulfilling the obligatory duty. The narration underscores the distinction between the mandatory Zakat and the voluntary generosity expected of the faithful.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man flees with his wealth from the Zakāt, and he buys a land with it, or a house. Is there anything upon him with regards to it?’ So heasws said: ‘No, and if he makes it to be an ornament or a carving, so there would be nothing upon him; and what he has prevented himself from its merit is more than what he prevented from a Right of Allahazwj if it happened to be in it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who runs away from paying Zakat by means of buying a piece of land or a house, if he still owes any Zakat. He (the Imam) said, ’No, he does not owe any Zakat even if he turns his asset into jewelries and silver; there is not anything on him. However, what he has denied his soul by the virtue of paying Zakat is much more than what he has saved by means of holding back the right of Allah that could have existed in his asset.”’
